english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice for asserting that something is true or strongly emphasizing an adjective or verb.
This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is really or genuinely so.
Use this as the all-purpose colloquial intensifier or disbelief marker.
This is the all-purpose everyday choice for saying that something is really or genuinely the case.
Use this when indeed means “truly,” and for emphatic “indeed,” especially before an adjective or verb.
Use this as the all-purpose colloquial intensifier for emphatic evaluations such as “absolutely brilliant.”
This is the all-purpose spoken choice when “literally” is loose, informal emphasis or filler.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for saying that something is genuinely or truly the case.
Use 真係 when “all right” emphatically confirms that something really happened or is certainly true.
Use this for emphatic or incredulous force when the English expletive does not need to sound vulgar.
Use this when “actually” means “really” and adds emphasis rather than simply correcting the listener.
For the actually or really sense, 真係 is the all-purpose spoken choice.
Use this when “properly” intensifies an adjective or reaction, as in being really tired.
Use 真係 before an adjective or evaluation when altogether means really or clearly, rather than completely.
Use this when the emphatic sense is “indeed” or “really,” rather than a rhetorical tag such as “係咪先.”
Use this when emphatically means ‘truly’ or ‘indeed’, especially in an informal assertion.
Use this as an emphatic intensifier in an exclamation where English uses “ever” for extra emphasis.
